title: Employee Growth and Enablement Ops Manual
author: Aisha Tan
body:
Overview
=======

Purpose: This manual documents the operational runbook for employee growth, cross-functional short rotations, skill-swap programs, benefits alignment, and the internal toolset required to make those programs reliable and repeatable. It is intended for people-ops, hiring managers, and engineering/product leads who run rotations, refresh role ladders, or onboard employees into growth pathways.

Scope: Covers program definitions, eligibility, tooling and access checklist, step-by-step processes for launching and closing swaps/rotations, success metrics, ownership, and FAQ. Does not replace team-level career conversations or formal promotion calibration processes (see related pages).

Quick summary
-------------
- Program types: Micro-rotations (2–6 weeks), Short rotations (1–3 months), Skill-swap pods (peer teaching cohorts), Mentorship pairings.
- Key systems: HRIS (Workday), Identity (Okta), Growth Portal (internal), IDP (Internal Developer Portal), Onboarding Bot (Slack), Access Portal (IAM console).
- Primary owners: people-ops (program design), hiring managers (role-level decisions), talent enablement (tooling & badges).

Program definitions and expected outcomes
--------------------------------------
1) Micro-rotation (2–6 weeks)
   - Goal: Rapid exposure to adjacent domain to inform role growth or project alignment.
   - Expected outcomes: two small deliverables, updated growth checklist, reflection artifact in Growth Portal.

2) Short rotation (1–3 months)
   - Goal: Operational contribution to another team while maintaining baseline responsibilities.
   - Expected outcomes: a cross-team PR/feature, skill evaluation signature from receiving manager, updated calibration notes.

3) Skill-swap pod (4–8 weeks)
   - Goal: Group learning where 3–6 participants teach and cross-learn a focused capability (e.g., observability, prompt engineering, infra IaC).
   - Expected outcomes: shared runbook, recorded teaching session, internal badge awarded.

Eligibility and selection criteria
--------------------------------
- All full-time employees with >6 months tenure are eligible for Micro-rotations; >12 months for Short rotations unless manager-approved.
- Manager endorsement required for any rotation longer than 6 weeks.
- People-ops will validate capacity and check for conflicts with hiring/critical project timelines.

Tooling and access matrix (required pre-rotation)
------------------------------------------------
| Tool / System         | Required Access Level        | Who Grants Access        | Notes |
|-----------------------|------------------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| Workday (HRIS)        | View / Update development plan | People-ops               | Used to record rotation in employee profile |
| Okta                 | Temporary app group access    | Identity team (IAM)      | Time-boxed LIFECYCLE token (default 90 days) |
| IDP (Internal Dev Portal) | Project repo read/write    | Receiving team lead      | Check repo ownership and CODEOWNERS |
| Growth Portal         | Program enrollment & evidence | Talent enablement        | Hosts reflection artifacts and badges |
| Access Portal (IAM)   | Cloud role (scoped)          | Receiving infra owner    | Ensure least-privilege and emergency revoke steps |
| Onboarding Bot (Slack) | Channel invites & reminders  | People-ops automation    | Used for reminders and surveys |

Pre-rotation checklist (manager + employee)
-------------------------------------------
1. Submit rotation request form in Growth Portal (see template).
2. Manager and receiving manager sign off on objectives and time allocation (% allocation expected).
3. People-ops confirms eligibility and dates, and triggers tooling access provisioning.
4. Talent enablement schedules a kickoff session and assigns peer mentor if requested.
5. Employee publishes a 1-page objective doc to Growth Portal before start.

Launch steps (detailed)
----------------------
1) Two weeks before start:
   - Employee: publish objective doc and risks/assumptions.
   - Sending manager: add rotation to team calendar and flag downstream owners.
   - Receiving manager: create on-boarding ticket in IDP and list required repos, infra, and contacts.
2) One week before start:
   - People-ops: provision Okta group membership and schedule access expiry.
   - Talent enablement: intro session (1hr) + 30-min technical ramp.
   - Employee: confirm allocation (time %) and remote/collaboration expectations.
3) First day:
   - 30-minute sync between sending and receiving manager, employee, and mentor.
   - Add reflection doc template to Growth Portal.

Close and handback process
--------------------------
1. Final deliverable submitted and reviewed by receiving manager.
2. Knowledge transfer session recorded and stored in IDP or team wiki.
3. Receiving manager completes a short evaluation (skills, impact, readiness) in Growth Portal.
4. People-ops revokes temporary access per Access Portal LIFECYCLE policy.
5. Employee updates personal development plan in Workday; sending manager reviews for next steps.

Success metrics and monitoring
-----------------------------
- Adoption: % of eligible population participating quarterly (target: 18% Q1 after launch).
- Impact: % of rotations resulting in at least one persistent cross-team artifact (target: 65%).
- Progression: % of participants with a role-ladder movement or formal skill badge within 12 months (target: 22%).
- Satisfaction: post-rotation CSAT (target: 4.2/5).

Reporting cadence and dashboards
-------------------------------
- People-ops maintains a monthly dashboard showing active rotations, tool provisioning status, and outcomes.
- Talent enablement publishes a quarterly summary with success stories, process improvements, and badge issuance metrics.

Cost and resourcing guidance
---------------------------
- Cost categories: People time (primary), tooling provisioning (negligible per rotation), and training content creation.
- Budget owner: people-ops (program-level) with per-team carveouts to be negotiated during QBR planning.

Governance and exceptions
-------------------------
- Any rotation that impacts a regulated customer or involves PII systems requires explicit security review and a temporary restricted confidentiality label.
- Exceptions to tenure or manager sign-off must be documented and approved by Head of People-ops and receiving manager.

Role ladder integration and badge issuance
-----------------------------------------
- Short rotations and skill-swap pods are mapped to career-ladder competency checkboxes in the Growth Portal.
- Upon validated completion, Talent enablement issues an internal badge that persists on the employee profile in Workday.
- Badges are advisory signals for promotion calibration but do not guarantee promotion.

Templates and examples
----------------------
- Rotation objective template (Growth Portal): title, outcome measures, success criteria, risks, key contacts, time allocation.
- Reflection template: what I learned, what I'd change, recommended next steps.
- Evaluation rubric (receiving manager): 1–5 scale across Contribution, Learning, Collaboration, and Documentation.

Ownership and escalation
------------------------
- Program owner: Head of People-ops (operational).
- Tooling owner: Talent enablement (Growth Portal and badges), Identity team (Okta lifecycle), Infrastructure owner (Access Portal).
- Escalation path: receiving manager -> sending manager -> Head of People-ops -> VP People.

FAQ (concise)
------------
Q: Can I do rotations while on parental leave?
A: No. Rotations require active work allocation and manager approval; exceptions handled case-by-case.

Q: Who pays for training materials?
A: People-ops covers standard program materials; teams may sponsor deep course licenses.

Q: Will rotation time count towards velocity commitments?
A: Teams should plan for reduced velocity and mark objectives accordingly; short rotations should not be scheduled during critical launch windows.

Appendix A — Example timeline (8-week short rotation)
---------------------------------------------------
Week 0: Approvals + tooling
Week 1: Kickoff + ramp
Week 2–6: Feature/impact work
Week 7: Knowledge transfer + final deliverable
Week 8: Evaluation + handback

Appendix B — Tool request CLI examples
-------------------------------------
# Example: Request Okta group membership (internal CLI)
redwood-iam request-group --user aisha.tan --group rot-receiving-team --expires 2029-05-01

# Example: Create rotation entry in Growth Portal (curl)
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GROWTH_PORTAL_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"employee":"aisha.tan","type":"short-rotation","start":"2029-04-01","end":"2029-06-01","objectives":"Observability baseline + dashboard"}' \ 
  https://growth.internal.redwood/api/v1/rotations

Contact and feedback
--------------------
For process questions or to propose changes to this manual, email people-ops@redwood.com or open a change request in the People-ops channel (Slack: #people-ops-change-requests).
